title: Date set for Horan inquest ; INQUEST: Man died in OPP custody
article: An inquest date has been set for Paul Horan, who died Sept. 24, 2010 at Bluewater Health's Charlotte Eleanor Englehart Site, following his involvement with the Ontario Provincial Police.
The inquest is mandatory under the Coroners Act.
It will examine the events surrounding the death of Horan, 43, and the jury could make recommendations aimed at preventing similar deaths.
It's expected to last nine days and hear from approximately 15 witnesses.
Horan died in Lambton OPP custody after being pulled over on Highway 402, near Forest Road, on Sept. 23, 2010.
He was taken into custody around 11:30 p.m. and was pronounced dead around 2:20 a.m. after going into convulsions in the back of an officer's cruiser.

The Special Investigations Unit (SIU) didn't find the officer guilty of any criminal liability. The SIU report stated Horan had ingested pills and refused to pull over in a vehicle with expired plates.
Horan's brother, Dave Horan, has said he doesn't agree with the SIU's findings.
The officer, who has never been named, declined to cooperate with the SIU investigation - nor was he required to - the provincial agency has said.
The inquest will begin at 10 a.m. on Aug. 14 at the Quality Inn, Point Edward, 751 Christina Street North.
Dr. Thomas Wilson will preside as inquest coroner, with Randy Evans counsel to the coroner.
The regional supervising coroner for West Region, Dr. Rick Mann, told The Observer in April:
"The purpose of the inquest is to answer five questions of who, when, where, by what means and manner, and the why of death."
